sections.text:
Autonomous racing provides a demanding testbed for collision avoidance under tight geometric and computational constraints.

Building on a recent conference contribution and a master's dissertation, LACART combines lookahead-based control barrier functions (CBFs), a relaxed control Lyapunov function (CLF), and quadratic programming (QP) to modify nominal vehicle commands for obstacle avoidance and reference tracking.

The method handles circular obstacles and track boundaries in a common optimisation layer. Comparative simulation results against Huang \emph{et al.} \cite{r9} show similar full-track paths and lower median computation times: 0.31 versus 0.33 ms per step and 0.023 versus 0.025 ms per QP solve.

The dissertation further demonstrates a 1:43-scale vehicle with camera-based estimation and wireless actuation at a reported 25 Hz control rate. We identify the conditions linking lookahead-point clearance to body clearance, illustrate hardware limitations, and propose a recorded demonstration of safety intervention and recovery.

The contribution targets ground-robot collision avoidance and real-time safety monitoring.

summary.en: LACART combines lookahead-based control barrier functions, a relaxed control Lyapunov function, and quadratic programming to adjust nominal commands for autonomous racing obstacle avoidance and reference tracking. It handles circular obstacles and track boundaries in one optimization layer. Comparative simulations report similar full-track paths to Huang et al. and lower median computation times. The dissertation also describes a 1:43-scale vehicle using camera-based estimation and wireless actuation at a reported 25 Hz. It discusses when lookahead-point clearance implies body clearance, hardware limitations, and a proposed recorded safety-intervention demonstration.

sections.text:
World Action Models (WAMs) have emerged as a promising approach to learning generalist robot policies using rich spatiotemporal priors from pre-trained video diffusion models.

A recent line of WAMs improves inference efficiency by conditioning a separate action decoder on intermediate future video representations extracted from a single denoising step, avoiding costly iterative denoising required for video generation. This design makes action prediction depend directly on the quality of these future representations.

In this paper, we introduce Future REpresentation learning via self-Distillation with temporal context (FRED), a framework that trains WAMs to improve the quality of future video representations from noise in a single denoising step.

Specifically, FRED uses self-distillation to predict future representations from noise, using representations extracted from ground-truth future observations as targets. We further condition the video model on historical observations, providing temporal context for predicting future representations better.

Across diverse real-world manipulation scenarios, FRED consistently outperforms competing WAMs.

It achieves particularly large gains on long-horizon and out-of-domain tasks under zero-shot environment generalization, and substantially improves human-to-robot skill transfer, reaching 50.0% task success on tasks absent from robot training data and demonstrated only in human videos, compared with 19.4% for the best competing WAM.

summary.en: The paper introduces FRED, a self-distillation framework that trains World Action Models to improve future video representations predicted from noise in a single denoising step. Representations extracted from ground-truth future observations serve as targets, while historical observations provide temporal context. Across diverse real-world manipulation scenarios, the authors report that FRED outperforms competing WAMs, with particularly large gains on long-horizon and out-of-domain zero-shot tasks and human-to-robot skill transfer. On tasks absent from robot training data and demonstrated only in human videos, reported success is 50.0%, versus 19.4% for the best competing WAM.
summary.zh: 论文提出 FRED，通过自蒸馏提升世界动作模型从噪声中一步生成未来视频表征的质量。方法以真实未来观测提取的表征为目标，并将历史观测作为时间上下文。作者报告，在多种真实操作场景中，FRED 整体优于其他世界动作模型；在长时程、分布外零样本泛化任务及人类到机器人的技能迁移中提升尤为明显。对于机器人训练数据中没有、仅由人类视频演示的任务，摘要称其成功率达到 50.0%，最佳对比模型为 19.4%。

sections.text:
What is considered safe for a robot operator during physical human-robot collaboration (HRC) is specified in corresponding HRC standards (e.g., ISO 10218-2:2025).The regime that allows collisions between the moving robot and the operator, called Power and Force Limiting (PFL), restricts the permissible contact forces.

Using the same fixed contact thresholds on the entire robot surface results unnecessary productivity losses, as the robot needs to stop even when impact forces are within limits.

Here we present a framework that decides whether the robot should interrupt motion based on estimated collision force computed individually for different parts of the robot body and dynamically on the fly, based on the Effective Mass (EM) of each robot link.

We performed experiments on a simulated and real collaborative robot arm (UR10e) with sensitive skin (AIRSKIN) for collision detection and isolation. To demonstrate the generality of our method, we added experiments on simulated KUKA LBR iiwa robot, where collision sensing draws on joint torque sensing.

On a mock pick-and-place scenario with both transient and quasi-static collisions, we show an increase in productivity over 45% from using the standard approach. The method is applicable to any robot for which the EF can be calculated.

summary.en: The paper presents a framework that estimates collision force dynamically for individual robot links based on effective mass, then decides whether motion should be interrupted. Experiments used a simulated and real UR10e with sensitive skin, and a simulated KUKA LBR iiwa using joint-torque sensing. In a mock pick-and-place scenario with transient and quasi-static collisions, the authors report productivity increased by over 45% compared with the standard approach. They state the method applies to robots whose effective mass can be calculated.
summary.zh: 论文提出一种基于机器人各连杆有效质量动态估算碰撞力的协作安全框架，用于判断是否中断运动，避免全身采用固定接触阈值造成不必要停机。作者在配备敏感皮肤的仿真及真实UR10e机械臂，以及使用关节力矩感知的仿真KUKA LBR iiwa上进行实验。在模拟抓取与放置场景中，涵盖瞬态和准静态碰撞；作者报告相较标准方法生产率提高超过45%，并称该方法适用于可计算有效质量的机器人。

sections.text:
Vision-language-action models (VLAs) map language instructions and visual observations to robot actions, showing strong capabilities across robotic manipulation tasks. However, in our probing experiment, we find that action representations near the action output do not fully preserve task-relevant visual grounding.

Motivated by this late-layer grounding gap, we introduce STAR, for STeering Action Representations, a training-free inference method for pre-trained VLAs.

STAR applies an exponential moving average over late-layer residual updates, allowing later action representations to inherit object-aware update directions from earlier layers without model updates or architectural changes.

It further uses recent proprioceptive states to adapt the mixing strength, using conservative mixing when execution dynamics change rapidly. Experiments on robot manipulation benchmarks show that STAR improves late-layer object awareness and increases average task success rates by 4.0 percentage points.

Our code is available at https://github.com/PKU-VaLuE-Lab/STAR.

summary.en: The authors identify a gap in which action representations near a vision-language-action model’s output do not fully preserve task-relevant visual grounding. They introduce STAR, a training-free inference method that applies an exponential moving average to late-layer residual updates, allowing later representations to inherit object-aware update directions. Recent proprioceptive states adjust the mixing strength, with conservative mixing during rapid changes in execution dynamics. Experiments on robot manipulation benchmarks show improved late-layer object awareness and a 4.0 percentage-point increase in average task success.
summary.zh: 论文指出，视觉语言动作模型靠近动作输出端的表示可能无法充分保留与任务相关的视觉信息，并提出无需训练的推理方法STAR。该方法对后层残差更新进行指数移动平均，使后续动作表示继承较早层的物体感知更新方向；同时利用近期本体感觉状态调整混合强度，在执行动态快速变化时采用保守混合。机器人操作基准实验显示，STAR提升了后层物体感知能力，平均任务成功率提高4.0个百分点。

sections.text:
Portable mobile-manipulation demonstrations can help alleviate data scarcity for embodied intelligence, but obtaining reliable, low-cost, and robot-free motion supervision from RGB observations remains challenging.

Existing approaches often rely on teleoperation or specialized devices equipped with additional sensing hardware, while directly using estimated visual odometry (VO) trajectories can introduce inconsistencies due to accumulated drift and imperfect motion supervision.

We present the Visual-Odometry-Conditioned Mobile Manipulation Interface (VOMMI), a portable demonstration collection and learning framework that connects portable RGB demonstrations to vision-language-action (VLA) post-training through offline trajectory reconstruction and online visual-motion conditioning.

VOMMI synchronizes body and hand views to capture navigation context and local object interactions without requiring human-robot kinematic correspondence calibration. R2-VO refines offline demonstration trajectories using sparse geometric anchors and produces causal local-motion tokens over multiple prediction horizons for online policy conditioning.

An action-group residual adapter incorporates these tokens only into the base branch. Experiments use a 500-trajectory portable for each task, with 75 trajectories held out for RGB-VO evaluation, and 200 robot demonstrations as references.

Our policy, post-trained only on portable demonstrations, achieves 18.2% lower base-velocity error than a policy trained with robot-collected demonstrations, while maintaining comparable end-effector translation accuracy.

Offline reconstruction reduces absolute trajectory errors for the body and hand streams by 24.6% on average relative to the best evaluated baseline for each stream. The complete system improves the mean success rate by 8.3 percentage points over OpenPI 0.5 across three real-robot tasks.

summary.en: The paper introduces VOMMI, a framework that connects portable RGB demonstrations to vision-language-action post-training through offline trajectory reconstruction and online visual-motion conditioning. It synchronizes body and hand views without calibrating human-robot kinematic correspondence. R2-VO refines trajectories with sparse geometric anchors and produces local-motion tokens for policy conditioning. In real-robot tasks, a policy post-trained only on portable demonstrations had 18.2% lower base-velocity error than one trained with robot-collected demonstrations, with comparable end-effector translation accuracy. The complete system improved mean success rate by 8.3 percentage points over OpenPI 0.5.
summary.zh: 论文提出VOMMI框架，将便携式RGB演示通过离线轨迹重建和在线视觉运动条件接入视觉语言动作模型后训练。它同步采集身体与手部视角，无需校准人机运动学对应关系；R2-VO利用稀疏几何锚点修正轨迹，并生成供策略使用的局部运动标记。真实机器人任务实验中，仅用便携演示后训练的策略，其底盘速度误差比机器人采集演示训练的策略低18.2%，末端平移精度相当；完整系统相较OpenPI 0.5平均成功率高8.3个百分点。

sections.text:
In recent years, massively parallelized rigid-body simulation has played a central role in robotics research, enabling rapid progress in areas such as reinforcement learning, stochastic optimal control, and randomized smoothing-based trajectory optimization.

Particularly in contact-rich settings, the scalability of such simulations in large part depends on well-optimized representations of collision geometry, often requiring a coarse approximation of the underlying surfaces using primitives such as spheres, capsules, cylinders, and boxes.

Whenever the complexity of the surfaces or the precision demands of the application render such approximations insufficient, it is instead necessary to employ mesh-mesh collisions, which impose a significant reduction in throughput.

This paper proposes a simulation framework designed from scratch to address this bottleneck, with novel routines for broadphase and narrowphase collision detection as well as the subsequent contact dynamics computation.

As experimentally validated, the framework matches existing well-established simulators in terms of physical faithfulness, and can achieve approximately an order of magnitude higher throughput in the detailed mesh-mesh collision setting that it specializes in. The source code is available at https://github.com/martius-lab/lodos.

summary.en: The paper presents Lodos, a lightweight rigid-body simulation framework for contact-rich interactions involving detailed meshes. It introduces new routines for broadphase and narrowphase collision detection and contact dynamics computation to address the throughput cost of mesh-mesh collisions. The authors report that experiments found its physical faithfulness comparable to established simulators, while throughput in the detailed mesh-mesh setting it targets was approximately an order of magnitude higher.
summary.zh: 论文提出 Lodos，一种面向精细网格接触交互的轻量级刚体仿真框架，旨在缓解网格间碰撞检测造成的吞吐量下降。框架设计了新的宽相位、窄相位碰撞检测及接触动力学计算方法。作者报告，实验验证其物理保真度与成熟仿真器相当；在其专长的精细网格碰撞场景中，吞吐量约提高一个数量级。

items.title: Lodos: A Lightweight Simulator Designed for Contact-Rich Interactions with Detailed Meshes

sections.text:
Recently, world-action models (WAMs) have emerged as a powerful framework for robot manipulation. By jointly modeling action generation and future observation prediction, WAMs can act and anticipate the outcomes of the actions.

However, existing WAMs typically rely on frozen pretrained encoders trained with reconstruction, which may not produce representations well suited for robot control. In this paper, we tackle the problem of learning physicallygrounded, control-relevant representations for WAMs.

We propose MDF++, a visuo-tactile world-action model that learns latent representations of multisensory observations end-to-end with a diffusion backbone. While naive joint training can lead to feature collapse, MDF++ introduces a multi-task learning strategy that leverages cross-modal correlations to learn task-relevant representations.

We evaluate MDF++ on a suite of contact-rich manipulation tasks, including realworld bolt screwing and nut mating, and show that it outperforms WAMs built on frozen pretrained representations by up to 50%.Additional videos are available on our website: jointmdf.github.io.

summary.en: The paper proposes MDF++, a visuo-tactile world-action model that learns latent representations of multisensory observations end to end using a diffusion backbone. To address feature collapse during joint training, it uses a multitask strategy that exploits cross-modal correlations. The authors evaluate it on contact-rich manipulation tasks, including real-world bolt screwing and nut mating, and report performance up to 50% better than world-action models using frozen pretrained representations.
summary.zh: 论文提出 MDF++，一种结合视觉与触觉的世界动作模型，使用扩散骨干网络端到端学习多感官观测的潜在表示。针对联合训练可能导致特征坍塌的问题，方法采用多任务学习策略，利用跨模态关联学习与任务相关的表示。作者在一组接触丰富的操作任务上进行评估，包括真实世界的螺栓拧紧和螺母配合，并报告其表现比采用冻结预训练表示的世界动作模型最高提升 50%。

items.title: MDF++: Visuo-Tactile World Action Model with End-to-end Representation Learning

sections.text:
Operators can state safety constraints for robots as prohibitions such as "do not put the bowl on the stove".We study whether OpenVLA follows such prohibitions and where it represents the goal it executes. The 10 tasks of LIBEROGoal share one scene, so we can label the goal that each rollout executes.

We combine closed-loop rollouts with activation patching, linear probes, activation steering and runtime monitors. On LIBERO-Goal, negation had no detectable effect on which task OpenVLA executed. The model executed the forbidden task in 79% of negated rollouts and completed 78% of plain tasks. A goal probe gives similar read-outs under "not X" and "X".

Activation patching shows that the first action depends mostly on the instruction tokens before layer 12 and on the last prompt token from layer 16 onward. A fixed steering vector at the instruction tokens at layer 8 redirected 12 of 18 rollouts. Fixed vectors and prefill patches at layers 12 to 20 redirected none of 158.

From layer 16, only patches at every decoded action token redirected the robot (15 of 18 rollouts at layer 24).When the instruction changes during a rollout, the layer-32 goal read-out detects non-compliance better than failure detectors, and an external probe on image and instruction features performs comparably.

These results support enforcing prohibitions outside the instruction and monitoring goal read-outs against the specification. Goal edits in OpenVLA should act before layer 12 or patch every action token.

summary.en: The paper studies whether OpenVLA follows prohibitions and where it represents its executed goal. In closed-loop LIBERO-Goal rollouts, negation had no detectable effect on task choice, and the model performed the forbidden task in 79% of negated rollouts. Activation interventions redirected 12 of 18 rollouts with a fixed steering vector at instruction tokens in layer 8, while fixed vectors and prefill patches at layers 12–20 redirected none of 158. The authors support enforcing prohibitions externally and monitoring goal representations against specifications.
summary.zh: 论文研究 OpenVLA 是否遵循“不要把碗放在炉子上”等禁令，以及模型内部如何表示执行目标。作者在 LIBERO-Goal 闭环测试中发现，否定指令对执行任务没有可检测影响；模型在 79% 的否定指令轨迹中仍执行禁做任务。激活干预显示，指令层 8 的固定引导向量可改变 18 次试验中的 12 次，而层 12 至 20 的固定向量或预填充干预均未改变 158 次试验中的结果。作者据此支持在指令之外落实禁令，并监测目标表示是否符合规范。

sections.text:
Aerial robots operating in cluttered environments may encounter openings narrower than their nominal width. Existing passively morphing drones reduce their width upon traversal, but they typically involve human-made designs, which can struggle to find the right balance among folding ratio, flight efficiency, and control tracking performance.

We introduce a closed-loop design method that jointly optimizes quadrotor geometry and the torque-deflection response of two passively folding arms driven by the success rate in simulation for contact-mediated gap traversal.

An optimization algorithm samples candidate designs that are evaluated in a contact-based simulation of the traversal task, where the task success rate is used as a feedback signal to sample progressively better designs over time.

The resulting prototype passively reduces its width from 31.3 to 14.1 cm and traverses a 15 cm wide opening at a 2 m/s reference speed. It also tolerates gap approach-angle errors of up to 30 degrees and folds through a 40 cm long confined passage.

Compared to a rigid twin, the soft configuration adds only 2 mm of position RMSE and less than 1% electrical power during contact-free flight. These results show that task-driven closed-loop design optimization can produce passively morphing airframes that are compact under contact, tolerant to approach error, and effectively rigid during nominal flight.

summary.en: The paper presents a closed-loop design optimization method that jointly tunes quadrotor geometry and the torque-deflection response of two passively folding arms, using simulated contact-mediated traversal success as feedback. The resulting prototype reduces its width from 31.3 cm to 14.1 cm and traverses a 15 cm opening at a 2 m/s reference speed. In the reported task evaluations, it tolerates approach-angle errors and passes through a confined passage. Compared with a rigid twin, the soft configuration adds 2 mm of position RMSE and less than 1% electrical power during contact-free flight.

sections.text:
Creative tool use is a fundamental human capability and an important step toward general-purpose embodied intelligence. It requires agents to reason about object affordances, physical constraints, and manipulation strategies, especially when standard tools are unavailable.

However, progress in this area is limited by the lack of real-world datasets that capture human tool-use behavior with sufficient scale, fidelity, and diversity. Existing benchmarks are often simulation-based, focus on simplified interactions, or lack detailed observations and annotations.

We introduce ToolDex, a large-scale egocentric-exocentric (ego-exo) human demonstration dataset for creative physical tool use. ToolDex captures scenarios in which humans select, adapt, and repurpose available objects as tools.

Using synchronized egocentric cameras and eight exocentric cameras, the dataset provides high-fidelity multi-view observations and rich annotations for hands, tools, target objects, and their deformable interactions.

Beyond data collection, we establish a benchmark suite characterizing three core capabilities: physical tool-use reasoning, sparse-view 3D and 4D reconstruction, and robot policy learning. ToolDex provides a foundation for studying human tool-use behavior and developing embodied agents that can adaptively use tools in complex real-world environments.

Dataset visualizations and benchmarking results are available at https://tooluse-dataset.github.io/.

summary.en: The paper introduces ToolDex, an egocentric-exocentric dataset of human demonstrations involving creative physical tool use, including selecting, adapting, and repurposing available objects. Synchronized egocentric cameras and eight exocentric cameras provide multi-view observations and annotations for hands, tools, target objects, and deformable interactions. The authors also establish benchmarks for physical tool-use reasoning, sparse-view 3D and 4D reconstruction, and robot policy learning. They describe the dataset as a resource for studying human tool use and developing embodied agents for complex real-world environments.
summary.zh: 论文介绍ToolDex，一个记录人类创造性实体工具使用的第一人称与第三人称示范数据集，涵盖选择、改造和重新利用现有物体作为工具的场景。数据通过同步的第一人称摄像机和八台外部摄像机采集，并提供手、工具、目标物体及其可变形交互的多视角观察与标注。作者还建立基准套件，用于评估物理工具使用推理、稀疏视角三维与四维重建，以及机器人策略学习。

sections.text:
This paper presents a soft robotic drummer for accurate and efficient drum rolls. High-frequency drum rolls require the "multi-bounce technique," where a drumstick bounces multiple times with a single stroke.

In robotic reproduction of this technique, the body's elasticity is key, while the fine motion during the stroke is also crucial for maximizing the potential of that elasticity.

Therefore, we design two tricks: i) Tap-Pull (TP) trick to increase the number of rebounds by adding a pulling motion after impact; and ii) Micro-Pulse (MP) trick to keep the drumming volume by injecting small oscillations during the stroke.

Due to the nonlinear complexity of soft embodiment, both tricks are efficiently tuned using Bayesian optimization in a data-driven manner for accomplishing the respective objectives quantified. We evaluated the optimized behaviors with soft and rigid end-effectors.

As a result, the soft TP achieved the highest bounce count (12.25 per stroke) with uniform intervals. The soft MP suppressed the volume decay, yielding 6.8-times higher acoustic efficiency compared to the rigid MP. These results indicate that the proposed tricks with the combination of elasticity and optimization can make robots play excellent drum rolls.

summary.en: The paper presents a soft robotic drummer for drum rolls and proposes two active motion tricks: Tap-Pull, which adds a pulling motion after impact, and Micro-Pulse, which injects small oscillations during a stroke. The authors tune the tricks with data-driven Bayesian optimization and evaluate the resulting behaviors using soft and rigid end-effectors. In the reported evaluations, soft Tap-Pull achieves 12.25 bounces per stroke with uniform intervals. Soft Micro-Pulse suppresses volume decay and has 6.8 times the acoustic efficiency of rigid Micro-Pulse.
summary.zh: 论文介绍一种用于鼓点连击的软体机器人鼓手，并提出两种主动动作技巧：击打后拉动鼓槌的Tap-Pull，以及行程中注入微小振荡的Micro-Pulse。作者通过数据驱动的贝叶斯优化调节两种技巧，并以软质和刚性末端执行器评估优化行为。实验结果中，软质Tap-Pull达到每击12.25次反弹且间隔均匀；软质Micro-Pulse抑制音量衰减，其声学效率为刚性Micro-Pulse的6.8倍。

items.title: Multi-bounce Drum Roll with Optimized Active Tricks to Leverage Soft Embodiment

sections.text:
Vision-language-action (VLA) models perform versatile manipulation tasks from language instructions, but their inference cost limits how fast a robot can respond in closed-loop control.

Visual token pruning reduces this cost; however, prior methods estimate token redundancy from encoded visual embeddings or attention, only after the visual encoder has processed the entire observation.

We propose \ours, a training-free token pruning method that moves the pruning decision ahead of the vision encoder by grounding it in a geometric prior derived from the robot's own action.

The action chunk predicted at the previous control step is already available before the current observation is encoded, and it specifies the end-effector and camera motion between consecutive observations.

The same action affects the two standard camera views asymmetrically: in the fixed third-person view, \ours retains patches along the projected end-effector trajectory together with semantic anchors, while in the wrist view, it prunes patches that remain unchanged after compensating for the action-induced camera motion.

Extensive experiments on two simulation environments (LIBERO and VLABench) and four real-robot tasks demonstrate that \ours achieves up to 1.61 $\times$ speedup and 59.5\% FLOPs reduction with negligible degradation in success rates.

summary.en: The paper presents ActPrune, a training-free method that uses geometric information from the robot’s previous predicted action to prune visual tokens before the current observation passes through the vision encoder. In a fixed third-person view, it retains patches near the projected end-effector trajectory and semantic anchors; in a wrist view, it removes patches unchanged after compensating for action-induced camera motion. Evaluations in LIBERO and VLABench simulations and on four real-robot tasks report up to 1.61× speedup and 59.5% fewer FLOPs, with negligible success-rate degradation.
summary.zh: 论文提出 ActPrune，一种无需训练、利用机器人上一控制步预测动作所含几何先验，在当前视觉观测进入视觉编码器前裁剪视觉 token 的方法。固定第三人称视角保留末端执行器轨迹投影附近的图像块及语义锚点；腕部视角则补偿动作引起的相机运动后，裁剪未变化的图像块。作者在 LIBERO、VLABench 两个仿真环境和四项真实机器人任务中评估，报告最高 1.61 倍加速、FLOPs 减少 59.5%，成功率仅有可忽略的下降。

items.title: ActPrune: Action-Grounded Visual Token Pruning for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Models

sections.text:
Assistive robots and search-and-rescue platforms require reliable human state sensing in smoke, darkness, and privacy-sensitive environments, where cameras and LiDAR may be unreliable Millimeter-wave radar offers an alternative that works without ambient light, penetrates smoke, and does not capture visual appearance.

However, the compact arrays that fit robot size, power, and cost budgets have limited apertures, producing joint-localization errors on the order of decimeters at a few meters, large enough to compromise the safety margins and tracking accuracy a robot depends on.

Existing pipelines reduce pose error through frame fusion, multiple viewpoints, return selection, or stronger estimators, but examine one technique at a time, without relating its effect to a shared measurement limit or separating gains from added information from gains from estimator completion.

We address this gap with a framework that models the human and environment as one time-varying scattering field and states a Cramer-Rao type error floor for joint localization as a function of bandwidth, aperture, signal-to-noise ratio, fused frame count, phase coherence, and visibility of retained returns.

We then use existing frame fusion, multi viewpoint, return selection, and pose estimation methods as matched probes of this floor rather than as competing pipelines.

Under the evaluated conditions, experiments on three datasets and a live deployment show these strategies move joint localization error in the predicted directions, for example lowering mean per-joint position error from about 97 to 65 mm with a second viewpoint, while a stronger estimator mainly lowers overall error by completing joints the measurement cannot resolve.

These results give the robotics community a principled basis for deciding whether to prioritize observation design or estimator capacity when deploying reliable mmWave human sensing.

summary.en: The paper studies limits on human joint localization with compact mmWave radar arrays for robot perception. It models people and the environment as a time-varying scattering field and derives a Cramer–Rao-type error floor related to bandwidth, aperture, signal-to-noise ratio, fused frame count, phase coherence, and visibility of retained returns. Tests on three datasets and in a live deployment examine frame fusion, multiple viewpoints, return selection, and pose estimation. The authors report that a second viewpoint lowers mean per-joint position error from about 97 to 65 mm; a stronger estimator mainly reduces overall error by completing unresolved joints.
summary.zh: 论文研究紧凑毫米波雷达阵列用于机器人感知人体状态时的定位误差限制，并提出一个将人体与环境视为时变散射场的框架，给出关节定位误差下限与带宽、孔径、信噪比、融合帧数、相位相干性及可见回波等因素的关系。作者在三个数据集和一次现场部署中评估帧融合、多视角、回波选择与姿态估计，称观测策略使误差按预测方向变化；增加第二视角将平均逐关节位置误差从约97毫米降至65毫米。较强估计器主要通过补全测量无法解析的关节降低整体误差。

sections.text:
Perceiving physical contact is fundamental to dexterous manipulation. While robots often rely on dedicated hardware tactile sensors, humans exhibit a remarkable ability to infer contact by integrating visual information with an innate sense of their body's pose and movement.

Inspired by this embodied perceptual skill, we investigate whether a robot can learn to infer contact from vision, an approach that also offers a scalable alternative to tactile hardware specifically for binary contact estimation, which faces practical challenges in cost, fragility, and integration.

We present NoContactNoWorries, a transformer-based multimodal framework that fuses RGB-D vision with the robot's proprioception to infer binary contact states as a pseudo-tactile signal for hand-object interactions.

We validate by training a single contact prediction model on multiple objects and show that the inferred contact signal supports downstream reinforcement learning agents for in-hand object reorientation, generalizing to novel objects.

Experiments in both simulation and on a real-world robot validate our approach, highlighting the feasibility of inferring contact from vision and proprioception. Project Page: https://soham2560.github.io/no-contact-no-worries/

summary.en: The paper introduces NoContactNoWorries, a transformer-based multimodal framework that combines RGB-D vision with robot proprioception to infer binary contact states during hand-object interaction, producing a pseudo-tactile signal. The approach is presented as an alternative to dedicated tactile hardware for binary contact estimation. The authors train one contact prediction model across multiple objects and report that its inferred signal supports reinforcement-learning agents performing in-hand object reorientation, with generalization to novel objects. Experiments in simulation and on a real-world robot are reported as validation of feasibility.
summary.zh: 论文提出 NoContactNoWorries，一种基于 Transformer 的多模态框架，融合 RGB-D 视觉与机器人本体感觉，以推断手与物体交互时的二元接触状态，并将其作为伪触觉信号。该方法旨在为二元接触估计提供一种不依赖专用触觉硬件的方案。作者用多个物体训练单一接触预测模型，并报告其推断信号可支持强化学习智能体进行手内物体重定向，且能泛化至新物体。仿真和真实机器人实验用于验证该方法的可行性。

items.title: NoContactNoWorries: Estimating Contact through Vision and Proprioception for In-Hand Dexterous Manipulation

sections.text:
Diagnosis and therapy in the pancreatobiliary tree are limited by access. Guidewires reach deep into the ducts but are blind, whereas cholangioscopes provide vision but are too large to readily enter the pancreatic body and tail, the cystic duct, or the gallbladder.

At the millimeter scale of these ducts, every function added to a steerable catheter competes with steering for cross-section and adds bending stiffness.

We present a 1.47-mm modular magnetic soft robotic catheter in which each function is built into the magnetic body, onto its surface, or onto the footprint of the camera, and we measured what each function costs in bending under bedside fields.

Imaging and fiber Bragg grating (FBG) shape sensing accounted for most of this cost, whereas a compliant gripper, magnetic anchoring balloons, and a micrometer-thick ultrasound-triggered release shell together reduced the tip angle at 8 mT only from 70{\deg} to 64{\deg}.

The anchoring balloon increased the gripping force about threefold without stiffening the catheter during navigation.

In live pigs, the robotic catheter performed operator-initiated task-autonomous cannulation of the native papilla without sphincterotomy and was teleoperated under onboard vision 75 mm into the pancreatic duct and, without a guidewire, through the cystic duct into the gallbladder, whose lumen it imaged.

Anchoring, grasping, and payload release were each demonstrated in vivo. Adding each function at a measured cost to steering allows a soft robot small enough for these ducts to intervene as well as navigate.

summary.en: The paper presents a 1.47-mm modular magnetic soft robotic catheter for visualized intervention in the pancreatobiliary tree. Its functions are integrated into the magnetic body, its surface, or the camera footprint, and their bending costs are measured under bedside fields. Imaging and fiber Bragg grating shape sensing account for most of the cost. A compliant gripper, anchoring balloons, and an ultrasound-triggered release shell reduce the tip angle at 8 mT from 70 to 64 degrees; the balloon increases gripping force about threefold without stiffening navigation. In live pigs, the catheter performs cannulation and teleoperated tasks in ducts and the gallbladder, with anchoring, grasping, and release demonstrated in vivo.
summary.zh: 论文介绍一种直径1.47毫米的模块化磁性软体机器人导管，面向胰胆管内可视化介入。导管将功能集成于磁性主体、表面或相机占用区域，并测量各功能在床旁磁场下对弯曲的影响。成像和光纤布拉格光栅形状传感贡献了大部分弯曲代价；顺应性抓手、磁性锚定球囊和超声触发释放外壳使8 mT下尖端角度从70度降至64度，锚定球囊则将抓力提高约三倍且导航时未增加刚度。活猪实验展示了乳头插管、胰管和胆囊内遥操作，以及锚定、抓取和释放。

sections.text:
Training end-to-end policies from image data to directly predict navigation actions for robotic systems has proven inherently difficult. Existing approaches often suffer from either the sim-to-real gap during policy transfer or limited action-labeled training data.

To address this problem, we introduce Visual Learned Distance (VLD), a scalable framework for image-goal navigation that decouples perception learning from policy learning.

We first train a self-supervised distance-to-goal predictor on about 3,000 hours of internet-scale and simulated video, providing a distance signal that a reinforcement learning (RL) policy can minimize.

The RL policy is trained separately in simulation using privileged geometric distances perturbed by GeoNoise, a learned noise model that reproduces the viewpoint- and overlap-dependent errors of the trained distance predictor.

At deployment, the policy consumes VLD predictions zero-shot, without retraining, inheriting ``where to go'' from large-scale visual training while retaining the robust navigation behaviors learned in simulation.

This error modeling is key to the transfer: with VLD inputs, GeoNoise-trained policies reach $58.7\%$ success on HM3D and $76.2\%$ on Gibson, whereas policies trained with generic temporally correlated noise collapse to $4.9\%$ and $11.5\%$.

On a physical robot, the VLD-driven policy succeeds in $88\%$ of trials, compared with $60\%$ for a strong end-to-end image-goal baseline that outperforms it in simulation. Our decoupled design thus provides an alternative and scalable path toward reliable navigation policies that transfer from simulation to the real world.

summary.en: The paper presents Visual Learned Distance (VLD), which separates perception learning from policy learning for image-goal navigation. A self-supervised goal-distance predictor is trained on about 3,000 hours of internet-scale and simulated video, while the reinforcement-learning policy is trained in simulation with geometrical distances perturbed by GeoNoise. The authors report success rates of 58.7% on HM3D and 76.2% on Gibson, and 88% in physical-robot trials, compared with 60% for an end-to-end image-goal baseline.
summary.zh: 论文提出视觉学习距离（VLD）框架，将图像目标导航中的感知学习与策略学习分开。作者用约3000小时网络及仿真视频训练自监督目标距离预测器，并在仿真中以加入GeoNoise扰动的几何距离训练强化学习策略，使策略部署时可直接使用VLD预测。作者报告，在HM3D和Gibson上的成功率分别为58.7%和76.2%；实体机器人试验成功率为88%，高于文中图像目标端到端基线的60%。

items.title: VLD: Visual Learned Distance as an Interface for Reinforcement Learning Navigation

sections.text:
We present Meituan-Robotics-0 (MR0), a vision-language-action foundation model and embodied-agent system for stationary-base desktop manipulation. MR0 combines 147 million vision-language samples with 15,060 hours of curated robot trajectories spanning 12 embodiments.

A three-stage training recipe aligns multimodal representations with robot behavior through discrete action-token pre-training, transfers these priors to continuous cross-embodiment control through flow-matching mid-training, and adapts the policy through real-world post-training.

We introduce Rollback, which pairs replaced policy segments with human corrections to provide positive and negative supervision for CFG-DAgger without value learning or advantage labeling. A unified end-effector interface supports heterogeneous embodiments, while asynchronous action-chunk merging maintains smooth execution under variable inference latency.

An event-driven agent maintains persistent task events and reassesses plans when progress or feasibility changes, enabling cross-task retrieval and conditional task resumption. MR0 achieves 93.6% success on RoboTwin 2.0 and ranks fifth in the RoboDojo VLA track.

Under matched HG-DAgger post-training, MR0 achieves higher average success rate and progress score than $\pi_{0.5}$ across three real-robot tasks. On Ethernet insertion, CFG-DAgger trained with Rollback data reaches 70% success and a progress score of 0.90.

Qualitative agent deployments demonstrate cross-task event retrieval and recovery from temporarily unsatisfied task conditions.

summary.en: The paper presents Meituan-Robotics-0 (MR0), a vision-language-action foundation model and agent system for stationary-base desktop manipulation. Its training uses discrete action-token pretraining, flow-matching mid-training across embodiments, and real-world post-training. The system also includes human-correction data, a unified end-effector interface, and event-driven task management. The authors report 93.6% success on RoboTwin 2.0, fifth place in the RoboDojo VLA track, and higher average success and progress scores than π0.5 across three real-robot tasks under matched HG-DAgger post-training.
summary.zh: 论文介绍Meituan-Robotics-0（MR0），一个面向固定底座桌面操作的视觉-语言-动作基础模型与具身智能体系统。其训练流程包含离散动作词元预训练、基于流匹配的跨本体中期训练和真实环境后训练；系统还采用Rollback纠正数据、统一末端执行器接口及事件驱动任务管理。作者报告，MR0在RoboTwin 2.0成功率为93.6%，在RoboDojo VLA赛道排名第五；匹配HG-DAgger后训练时，其三项真实机器人任务的平均成功率和进度分数高于π0.5。定性部署展示了跨任务事件检索及条件暂不可满足时的恢复。

sections.text:
Human videos contain abundant object-manipulation demonstrations, but they do not directly provide motion cues that a robot can follow. We present HOC2R, a Hand-Object Contact trajectory extractor for Robot motion that combines frozen DINOv3 and SAM 2.1 features with learned heads for hand-object association and contact localization.

HOC2R supports two modes: count-aware automation that detects, counts, and localizes visible contacts in untrimmed videos, and fixed-two localization for two-finger grippers when contact frames are known.

On a 30-task point-annotated benchmark, count-aware automation improves contact-count accuracy from 58.1% to 71.4% and reduces mean localization distance from 19.81 to 10.46 pixels relative to an adapted VRB2 baseline. On seven unseen RGB-D rollouts, a five-task fixed-two checkpoint reduces mean localization distance from 67.67 to 27.02 pixels.

Across six robot evaluation sequences, the 30-task fixed-two checkpoint produces four feasible trajectories and succeeds on three tasks, compared with two feasible trajectories and one successful task for each adapted baseline.

HOC2R is competitive in the evaluated single-hand scenes, robust to the hand-color shift, and strongest in the evaluated multi-hand scenes. These results support HOC2R as a practical pseudo-labeling method for extracting robot-usable contact trajectories from human demonstrations.

summary.en: The paper introduces HOC2R, which extracts hand-object contact trajectories from human manipulation videos for robot use. It combines frozen DINOv3 and SAM 2.1 features with learned heads for hand-object association and contact localization. Its modes support automatic contact detection, counting, and localization in untrimmed video, or localization of two gripper contacts when frames are known. On a 30-task annotated benchmark, the authors report improved count accuracy and lower localization distance than an adapted VRB2 baseline; in robot evaluations, a fixed-two checkpoint yielded four feasible trajectories and succeeded on three tasks.
summary.zh: 论文提出HOC2R，从人类操作视频中提取可供机器人使用的手-物接触轨迹。该方法结合冻结的DINOv3和SAM 2.1特征，以及用于手物关联和接触定位的学习头；支持对未剪辑视频自动检测、计数和定位接触，也支持已知接触帧时定位双指夹爪的两个接触点。在30项任务的点标注基准上，作者报告自动模式相较适配的VRB2基线提高接触计数准确率并降低定位距离；机器人评估中，固定双点模型产生4条可行轨迹并完成3项任务。

sections.text:
Evaluating robot policies before deployment typically requires producing new trajectories through real-world execution, simulators, or learned world models. These rollout-based approaches impose infrastructure requirements; simulator and world-model evaluators additionally face prediction errors that can compound over the evaluation horizon.

In this paper, we study off-policy evaluation as an alternative to rollout-based robot-policy evaluation methods.

Specifically, we introduce RoboFQE, an evaluator that estimates the discounted expected return of a target policy from offline robot trajectories without estimating a behavior-policy density, combining fitted Q-evaluation with a pretrained vision foundation model and learned terminal success annotation to bridge the gap between standard OPE benchmarks and continuous-control visual manipulation.

Controlled experiments across simulated and real-world manipulation tasks show that RoboFQE produces accurate discounted-return estimates and preserves policy rankings even on long-horizon manipulation tasks where video world-model evaluators are degraded by autoregressive prediction errors.

Ablation experiments show that pretrained vision encoders substantially outperform from-scratch alternatives, particularly on long-horizon tasks, and that learned terminal success annotation enables evaluation without ground-truth reward labels with only slight reduction of accuracy.

summary.en: The paper studies evaluating visual robot policies from offline trajectories, avoiding the need to generate new rollouts for evaluation. RoboFQE combines fitted Q-evaluation, a pretrained vision foundation model, and learned terminal-success annotation to estimate a target policy’s discounted expected return without estimating behavior-policy density. Controlled experiments on simulated and real-world manipulation tasks show accurate estimates and preserved policy rankings, including on long-horizon tasks. The authors report that video world-model evaluators degrade there from autoregressive prediction errors; ablations favor pretrained visual encoders and find only a slight accuracy reduction without ground-truth reward labels.
summary.zh: 论文研究利用离线机器人轨迹评估视觉策略，以避免评估时执行新轨迹。作者提出RoboFQE，通过拟合Q评估、预训练视觉基础模型和学习得到的终止成功标注，估计目标策略的折扣期望回报，无需估计行为策略密度。模拟和真实操作任务的受控实验显示，RoboFQE能给出准确的回报估计并保留策略排序，包括长时程任务；作者称视频世界模型评估器在此类任务中会受自回归预测误差影响。消融实验还显示，预训练视觉编码器优于从头训练方案，而学习终止成功标注可在没有真实奖励标签时进行评估，准确度略有下降。

items.title: RoboFQE: Rollout-Free Evaluation of Visual Robot Policies from Offline Trajectories

When should a robot look at the cup, and when at the portafilter? Spatial-reasoning benchmarks evaluate whether a model can describe a scene, but manipulation needs something more specific: the ability to acquire the particular evidence that makes the current command executable.

Across three domains--coffee workstation, drawer/cabinet, and microwave/appliance--the benchmark provides 860 frozen evaluation cases; expanding across methods, budgets, and inference repeats yields more than 115,000 evaluator episodes under two protocols: closed-loop actionability and same-object functional out-of-distribution generalization.

Each case pairs a set of candidate RGB views with a manipulation command, shared scripted skills, and hidden postconditions, so the benchmark directly measures whether a view-selection policy acquires the observations its command actually needs.

We also provide a diagnostic reference pipeline that maintains a spatial-functional belief state and ranks views by missing evidence. At primary budget settings, this pipeline reaches 98.8% closed-loop and 98.9% functional-OOD success; ablating the functional or command-binding components collapses performance to near zero.

Seven vision-language models, evaluated on the same cases, reach only 26-43%.Replacing the reference pipeline's coverage metadata with frozen RGB-derived scores preserves 98.5%/98.9% success; shuffling the visual scores collapses it to 15%/11%, confirming that the result depends on image content.

These gaps suggest that spatial belief for manipulation should be evaluated not by scene-level completeness, but by whether it acquires the evidence the current command requires.

It covers coffee workstations, drawers and cabinets, and microwave or appliance settings, using frozen cases and two protocols: closed-loop actionability and same-object functional out-of-distribution generalization. Cases pair candidate RGB views and commands with scripted skills and hidden postconditions. A diagnostic reference pipeline achieves 98.8% closed-loop and 98.9% functional-OOD success at primary budgets; ablations fall near zero, while seven vision-language models achieve 26–43%. The authors argue evaluation should focus on acquiring command-required evidence rather than scene completeness.

sections.text:
Agentic robotics asks coding agents to implement and iteratively improve robot policies from simulated and real-world physical interactions.

We study the self-learning loop of agentic robotics through a controlled simulation study spanning nine manipulation tasks, 631 different experiment configurations, and 28K coding agent rollouts, systematically varying model capability, skill priors, feedback structure, and curriculum.

The experiment data suggests that the bottleneck is often not the access to sufficient information, but interpreting it into the right policy update.

Across these factors, a successful self-learning loop depends on how effectively agents attribute failures, reason task-relevant spatial and geometric structure, and selectively restructure code to improve policies.

summary.en: This controlled simulation study examines self-learning in agentic robotics, where coding agents implement and iteratively improve robot policies using simulated and real-world physical interactions. It spans nine manipulation tasks and varies model capability, skill priors, feedback structure, and curriculum. The authors report that the bottleneck is often not access to enough information, but interpreting that information into an appropriate policy update. They associate successful learning loops with failure attribution, reasoning about task-relevant spatial and geometric structure, and selectively restructuring code.
summary.zh: 本文通过受控仿真研究考察具身机器人智能体的自学习过程：编码智能体依据模拟及真实物理交互实现并迭代改进机器人策略。实验覆盖九项操作任务，并系统改变模型能力、技能先验、反馈结构和课程设置。作者报告，瓶颈往往不在信息是否充足，而在于能否将信息解释为恰当的策略更新。成功的自学习循环取决于智能体归因失败、推理任务相关的空间与几何结构，以及有选择地重组代码以改进策略的能力。

sections.text:
Circumnavigating a stationary target with a team of robots requires each robot to hold its own standoff distance, to stay evenly spaced from its neighbours, and to avoid collisions with the target and with each other at every instant. The task becomes arduous when the robots are assigned different orbital radii, as their sensors or roles may demand.

This paper presents a safety-critical control framework for this problem. Each robot commands both its acceleration and its turn-rate, measures only its distance to the target, and exchanges information only with its two ring neighbours. The design has three features.

First, a structural property of the model lets one control law serve every robot regardless of its assigned radius. Second, the acceleration drives each radius exactly to its target, while the turn-rate balances the formation with the neighbours.

Third, a higher-order control-barrier-function quadratic program enforces target, geofence, and inter-robot safety on both inputs at once; it leaves the nominal controller untouched away from the constraints and stays valid while the unmeasured range rate is still being estimated. Simulations confirm these guarantees.

In a comparison, the closest existing multi-orbit design, even with full state information, violates both the target standoff and the inter-robot margin, whereas the proposed controller does not.

summary.en: The paper proposes a safety-critical framework for nonholonomic multi-robot circumnavigation on heterogeneous orbits. Each robot measures only target range and communicates with its two ring neighbors. A shared control law handles different orbital radii: acceleration regulates standoff distance, while turn rate coordinates formation. A higher-order control-barrier-function quadratic program constrains both inputs for target, geofence, and inter-robot safety. Simulations support the guarantees; a comparison reports violations by an existing method.
summary.zh: 论文提出一种用于非完整约束多机器人异轨道绕行的安全控制框架。机器人只测量目标距离，并与环上的两个邻居交换信息；统一控制律适用于不同轨道半径，加速度调节目标距离，转向率协调队形。高阶控制屏障函数二次规划同时约束两种输入，以保证目标、地理围栏和机器人间安全；仿真支持其安全保证，且比较中现有方法违反目标距离和机器人间隔约束。

items.title: Safe Circumnavigation on Heterogeneous Orbits: A Range-Only HOCBF-QP Framework for Nonholonomic Multi-Agent Systems

sections.text:
Many applications, such as surveying, autonomous navigation, robotics and augmented reality, require accurate pose information with respect to a reference frame. Visual localization can complement GNSS positioning, whose availability and accuracy are often limited.

However, the accuracy potential of visual localization has not yet been systematically investigated against survey-grade requirements, and no publicly available large-scale outdoor dataset provides ground-truth poses accurate enough for such an investigation. We address both gaps. First, we present the FHNW Muttenz dataset.

It covers a contiguous 10 km street network, mapped in two mobile mapping campaigns about 1.5 years apart, and comprises high-resolution reference imagery as well as query sequences from four cameras in five scenes. The two campaigns are co-registered to each other with an accuracy of 5 mm.

Co-registration of the query images to the reference imagery yields ground-truth poses accurate to 6-9 mm in position and well below 0.1{\deg} in orientation. All images are georeferenced with an accuracy of about 2.5 cm.

Second, we use this dataset to systematically evaluate sparse feature-based visual localization with a modular pipeline built from established components, using the high-resolution reference imagery directly as the scene representation.

For daytime imagery and pre-calibrated cameras, the median pose errors with respect to the reference imagery are 1-5 cm in translation and 0.03-0.1{\deg} in rotation. Given an accurately georeferenced scene representation, visual localization not only approaches the accuracy of survey-grade GNSS positioning but also provides full orientation information.

The dataset is publicly available at https://fhnw-muttenz-vl-dataset.github.io/

summary.en: The paper presents the FHNW Muttenz dataset to study visual localization accuracy against survey-grade requirements. It contains reference imagery from two mobile mapping campaigns and query sequences from four cameras across five scenes; the authors report millimeter-level ground-truth poses. They also evaluate a modular sparse feature-based localization pipeline using the reference imagery as the scene representation. For daytime images and pre-calibrated cameras, the reported median translation errors are 1–5 cm and rotation errors are 0.03–0.1 degrees.
summary.zh: 论文介绍 FHNW Muttenz 数据集，用于评估视觉定位相对于测绘级要求的精度。数据集覆盖连续街道网络，包含两次移动测绘采集的参考影像及四台相机在五个场景中的查询序列；作者称其提供毫米级位姿真值。研究还用模块化稀疏特征流程进行系统评估。在白天影像和预标定相机条件下，报告的中位平移误差为厘米级、旋转误差低于0.1度。

items.title: Accuracy potential of visual localization exploiting high-end street-level imagery

sections.text:
Scaling up visual humanoid loco-manipulation skill acquisition requires reducing the human effort needed as tasks and spatial configurations expand, particularly in demonstration collection and task-specific training design.

We present SUGARv2, a unified framework for learning diverse visual humanoid loco-manipulation skills through interaction reference synthesis and a shared training pipeline. To obtain diverse references at low cost, we adapt reusable task templates to different spatial configurations, synthesizing coordinated robot and object motions.

To reduce task-specific reward design and training effort, we use reference-based imitation as a common learning objective across tasks.

We first train privileged teachers to execute these references, then train visual policies through teacher distillation and reinforcement learning with the same reference-based mimic rewards, using diverse object instances and visual domain randomization to support visual generalization and sim-to-real transfer.

Across five humanoid loco-manipulation tasks, SUGARv2 achieves a mean success rate of 91.0% in simulation. Deployment on a real humanoid robot further demonstrates successful sim-to-real transfer for whole-body manipulation. These results demonstrate the framework's potential for learning diverse visual humanoid loco-manipulation skills.

summary.en: SUGARv2 is a framework for learning visual humanoid loco-manipulation skills using synthesized interaction references and a shared training pipeline. Reusable task templates generate coordinated robot and object motions for different spatial configurations, while reference-based imitation provides a common objective. Visual policies are trained through teacher distillation and reinforcement learning, with varied objects and visual domain randomization. Across five tasks, the reported mean simulation success rate is 91.0%; deployment on a real humanoid demonstrates sim-to-real transfer for whole-body manipulation.
summary.zh: 论文提出 SUGARv2，通过合成交互参考动作和共享训练流程学习多样化的人形机器人视觉移动操作技能。方法将可复用任务模板适配到不同空间配置，以参考动作模仿作为共同学习目标，再通过教师蒸馏和强化学习训练视觉策略，并采用多样物体实例及视觉域随机化。五项任务的仿真平均成功率为91.0%；真实人形机器人部署展示了全身操作的仿真到现实迁移。

items.title: SUGARv2: Learning Diverse Visual Humanoid Loco-Manipulation Skills from Synthesized Interaction References

A grid precomputed per footprint returns, in one pass over the local obstacles, a certified free distance along every candidate

sections.text:
Global planners for ground vehicles usually approximate the vehicle by a disk, trading safety against conservativeness, while exact-footprint checking pays for every candidate motion, pose, and footprint edge.

We present TPS-A*, a lattice planner whose edges are kinematically feasible trajectories from parameterized trajectory generators, built on certified collision checking in trajectory parameter space.

A grid precomputed per footprint returns, in one pass over the local obstacles, a certified free distance along every candidate trajectory, so the per-node collision cost is independent of footprint complexity and trajectory count.

We prove that this grid never overestimates the free distance of the continuously swept, possibly non-convex footprint, and state the planner's guarantees: collision-free paths and bounded suboptimality relative to its lattice abstraction. Goals with or without heading are reached exactly by Reeds-Shepp shots certified as trajectories of the same generators.

An exact independent test finds no collision in its paths.

On 300 cluttered worlds, with the true footprint and the same goal pose for all planners, it solves every query with a collision-free goal pose in a median of three milliseconds on an AMD Ryzen 7 2700X, on par with hybrid A*, 45\% of whose paths overlap obstacles, and nearly sixty times faster than a state-lattice planner, the only other collision-free one; with position goals, eighty-nine times faster than hybrid A*.

It matches hybrid A* in automated parking and on narrow doorways, docks a non-convex fork footprint that no convex model admits, and drove a real robot across a university campus among people.

summary.en: The paper presents TPS-A*, a lattice planner using certified collision checking in trajectory parameter space. The authors state that its footprint-specific precomputed grid certifies free distance for continuously swept, possibly non-convex footprints, with collision-free paths and bounded suboptimality relative to the lattice abstraction. An independent exact test found no collisions in its paths. In 300 cluttered simulated worlds, it solved every query with a collision-free goal pose using the true footprint, with a median runtime of three milliseconds. The authors also report parking, narrow-doorway, fork-footprint, and campus robot results.
summary.zh: 论文提出 TPS-A*，一种基于轨迹参数空间认证碰撞检测的栅格规划器。作者称，其按足迹预计算的网格可认证连续扫掠的非凸足迹安全距离，并保证路径无碰撞及相对栅格抽象的有界次优性；独立精确测试未发现路径碰撞。在300个杂乱仿真场景中，使用真实足迹的规划器均解决了具有无碰撞目标姿态的查询，中位耗时3毫秒。作者还报告其在自动泊车、窄门和非凸叉车足迹任务中的表现，以及机器人在大学校园的真实运行。

items.title: TPS-A*: Path Planning for Any-Shape Vehicles with Certified Collision Checking in Trajectory Parameter Space

sections.text:
Recent progress in embodied robotics is bringing robots closer to deployment in homes, as vision-language models (VLMs) are demonstrating significant advances in reasoning, making VLM-driven robots promising home assistant agents.

These agents will often be introduced into homes that already have cameras, Internet of Things (IoT) devices, and residents with wearables.

To fulfill their potential, they need to integrate with existing smart infrastructure and reason through ambiguous scenarios: a smoke alarm may come from a pan about to ignite, a pan already on fire, a resident cooking or a faulty sensor, and each calls for a different response.

To that end, we introduce HomeLoop, a simulation framework and benchmark built on Isaac Sim that combines robot bodies, networked devices and wearables, simulated residents and visitors, faulty sensors, and hazards that evolve over time.

Our benchmark is composed of 20 tasks across five families grounded in real-world household hazards and needs, and designed so that the same alert can have different causes. A runtime monitor scores each episode with temporal-logic checks on the final outcome and the actions along the way, and every action carries a predefined cost.

We evaluate six open-weight and proprietary VLMs.

The best achieves a family-balanced score of 61.9%, and across models we see a pattern of over-reaction: failed episodes involving prohibited interventions outnumber those involving missed required interventions by more than two to one, with models often shutting off the stove before investigating the alarm's cause.

HomeLoop is an extensible foundation intended for use in research on robot-IoT coordination, long-term memory, proactive assistance, and privacy-safety trade-offs. HomeLoop will be released with 2,100 home layouts that can be automatically furnished in diverse configurations, five robot bodies and 20 networked device types.

summary.en: The paper introduces HomeLoop, an Isaac Sim framework and benchmark for coordinating domestic robots with IoT infrastructure. It models robot bodies, networked devices and wearables, residents and visitors, faulty sensors, and evolving hazards. Its 20 tasks span five families; the same alert can have different causes, and episodes are scored with temporal-logic checks and predefined action costs. Evaluations of six open-weight and proprietary VLMs yielded a best family-balanced score of 61.9%. Across models, failures involving prohibited interventions were more than twice as common as missed required interventions. The authors intend HomeLoop to support further research.
summary.zh: 论文介绍 HomeLoop，这是基于 Isaac Sim 的家庭机器人与物联网协同仿真框架和基准，包含机器人、联网设备、可穿戴设备、居民与访客、故障传感器及动态演化的危险情境。基准涵盖五类共20项任务，同一警报可对应不同原因，并通过时序逻辑和预设行动成本评分。对六种开源权重及专有视觉语言模型的评估中，最佳家庭任务均衡得分为61.9%；总体上，涉及违规干预的失败次数超过漏做必要干预的两倍。作者称该框架旨在支持相关研究，并计划随之发布多种家庭布局、机器人机体和联网设备类型。

items.title: HomeLoop: A Simulation Framework and Benchmark for Robot-IoT Coordination in Everyday Domestic Assistance and Safety

sections.text:
Real-world robot deployment requires adapting learned policies to unseen obstacles without collecting new demonstrations or retraining.

Existing policy-level guidance often applies obstacle corrections independently at individual horizon steps, which may address local obstacle violations but fail to coordinate the action sequence into a complete, task-directed detour.

How obstacle responses should be propagated across the action horizon to coordinate complete, task-directed avoidance motion remains underexplored. We introduce an inferencetime obstacle-guidance framework for pretrained relative-action diffusion policies.

It rolls out cumulative relative actions into a workspace trajectory, evaluates obstacle interactions along the trajectory with an SDF-based obstacle model, and propagates each obstacle response to all contributing action increments during denoising.

Real-robot experiments across seven obstacleconstrained scenarios spanning four manipulation tasks show that our method achieves 105/140 (75.0%) collision-free task successes, compared with 8/140 (5.7%) for absolute-action pointwise guidance.

Ablations show that the relative-action horizoncoupled formulation provides the larger observed improvement across both obstacle models.

summary.en: The paper proposes an inference-time obstacle-guidance method for pretrained relative-action diffusion policies. It rolls cumulative relative actions into a workspace trajectory, evaluates obstacle interactions with a signed-distance-field model, and propagates obstacle responses to contributing action increments during denoising to coordinate avoidance across the action horizon. In real-robot experiments covering seven obstacle-constrained scenarios and four manipulation tasks, the method achieved 105 of 140 collision-free task successes (75.0%), compared with 8 of 140 (5.7%) for absolute-action pointwise guidance. Ablations indicate that the relative-action, horizon-coupled formulation provided the larger observed improvement.

sections.text:
Non-prehensile robot manipulation is challenging due to discontinuous, long-horizon interactions between the robot and the objects it manipulates. Sampling-based model predictive control methods are effective with discontinuous contact but face challenges with finding promising trajectories in long-horizon planning.

We propose a closed-loop object-informed (CLOI) method that splits the problem into object-level planning to find long-horizon object poses that lead the object to its goal, and robot-level planning to select robot actions that follow those poses.

We use model predictive path integral (MPPI) control to solve the subproblems and couple their solutions through consensus on the object poses using the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM).The object plan is revised toward robot-realizable object trajectories, while the robot plan is aligned with the object poses the task requires.

In planar pushing tasks with obstacles using an xArm6 manipulator, CLOI increases the success rate by 35% in simulation and 43% on hardware, compared to standard MPPI given the same computational budget.

summary.en: The paper proposes closed-loop object-informed control (CLOI) for non-prehensile manipulation involving long-horizon, discontinuous contact. It separates planning into object-level goal poses and robot-level actions, solves the subproblems with MPPI, and couples them through consensus on object poses using ADMM. This revises object plans toward robot-realizable trajectories and aligns robot plans with task-required poses. In planar pushing tasks with obstacles using an xArm6 manipulator, CLOI increased success rates by 35% in simulation and 43% on hardware compared with standard MPPI under the same computational budget.
summary.zh: 论文提出闭环物体知情控制方法 CLOI，用于处理非抓取式机器人操作中的长时域、不连续接触问题。方法将规划分为物体层级的目标姿态规划和机器人层级的动作规划，以 MPPI 分别求解，并通过 ADMM 在物体姿态上协调两者，使物体计划贴近机器人可实现的轨迹、机器人计划对齐任务所需姿态。在使用 xArm6 机械臂、带障碍物的平面推动任务中，相较计算预算相同的标准 MPPI，作者报告 CLOI 在仿真中成功率提高35%，在硬件实验中提高43%。

sections.text:
We focus on the problem of high-speed multi-robot navigation in cluttered spaces with tight spatial constraints. A key challenge is balancing safety with agility, as existing methods often trade one for the other (slowing down near a bottleneck to avoid collisions versus failing to swerve in time at high speeds), especially for car-like systems.

Our approach belongs to the family of formation control methods, in which Ackermann-steering agents coordinate while navigating tight spaces. However, current formation control techniques rely on rigid, pre-defined shapes and transitions that depend on initial conditions, the environment, and vehicle dynamics, and are impractical to maintain at high speeds.

For example, agents passing through a small gap must first form a square, transform into a line using analytical equations, and then return to a square. In contrast, our approach is inspired by a droplet of water that continuously adapts its shape to the space it flows through without slowing down.

We propose a hierarchical algorithm in which, at the high level, a reinforcement learning policy produces a dynamic, blob-like elliptical patch that morphs its shape in real time, squeezing, stretching, and orienting itself around obstacles and through tight spaces.

At the low level, the robots are controlled via distributed model predictive control (DMPC) to stay inside the patch, which acts as a soft forcing function, while avoiding collisions with each other. We evaluate our approach, FastFunnels, on simulated F1TENTH racing cars across 14 scenarios with N=1 to N=6 robots, averaged over 20 trials each.

FastFunnels achieves an 89% completion rate at 7.73 m/s, while all baselines either fail to complete the track or succeed only at very low speeds (0.07-1.79 m/s, about 40% completion rate).

summary.en: The paper presents FastFunnels for high-speed multi-robot navigation in narrow, cluttered spaces. A high-level reinforcement learning policy adjusts an elliptical region in real time, while distributed model predictive control keeps robots inside it and avoids inter-robot collisions. The authors evaluate the method in simulation with F1TENTH cars across 14 scenarios, using one to six robots and 20 trials per setting. sections.text:
We introduce a data-efficient distributed Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) framework for multi-robot operation in GPS-denied and communication-constrained environments.

The framework is designed for teams of robots equipped with LiDAR, cameras, and inertial sensors, where robots may operate from independently initialized local coordinate frames and share only limited spatial overlap.

Our approach constructs a scene graph by using fused RGB-LiDAR point clouds to generate both a semantically segmented point cloud layer, and a layer of discrete bounded objects, to accompany estimated robot trajectories. Scene graph matching is performed collaboratively through exchanging and matching object data with neighboring robots.

To maximize communication efficiency, we utilize a multi-step data exchange and optimization process. We demonstrate the effectiveness and communication efficiency of the proposed approach using real-world datasets containing limited trajectory overlap, viewpoint variation, repeated structures, and degraded visual conditions.

summary.en: The paper introduces a distributed SLAM framework for multi-robot teams operating without GPS and under communication constraints. It targets settings with independently initialized local coordinate frames and limited spatial overlap. The framework fuses RGB and LiDAR point clouds into scene graphs containing semantic point-cloud layers, discrete bounded objects, and estimated trajectories. Robots collaboratively exchange and match object data with neighbors through a multi-step communication and optimization process. The authors demonstrate effectiveness and communication efficiency on real-world datasets with limited overlap, viewpoint changes, repeated structures, and degraded visual conditions.

sections.text:
Generative sequence models are often trained to plan motion in physical domains, from robotics to mechanical simulations. When constructing a dataset to train such a model, engineers may curate demonstrations to specify how trajectories should be distributed over a physical quantity like travel distance or mechanical energy.

For example, a roboticist building a maze navigation agent might choose demonstrations whose travel distances cover a fixed range uniformly, hoping to constrain the agent's expected power usage.

We find that standard deep learning can violate this intent: each generated trajectory can seem plausible on its own, but the aggregate distribution over the physical quantity is wrong. We call this failure physical misgeneralization.

In this work, we identify and formalize the problem, develop and validate an account of its mechanism, and use that account to compare and design mitigations.

Using controlled synthetic tasks, we show that physical misgeneralization arises when local errors typical of the model class propagate through the physical measurement to shift the recovered distribution.

We estimate these errors with a data deviation kernel, and we use it to predict which physical quantity values gain or lose mass under real diffusion sequence models trained on both toy and applied trajectory generation tasks. Finally, our mechanistic interpretation helps identify which mitigations are structurally promising.

We first compare interventions that modify the dataset and generative interface, then show that the mechanistic understanding we develop throughout this paper suggests a novel way to construct data representations informed by the kernel.

We show that our proposed mitigation, which transforms the coordinate system under which the generator learns and samples, effectively reduces quantity drift.

summary.en: The paper studies physical misgeneralization in generative sequence models: individual trajectories may appear plausible while their aggregate distribution over quantities such as travel distance or mechanical energy departs from the intended training distribution. The authors formalize the problem and propose that local errors typical of a model class propagate through physical measurement, shifting the recovered distribution. Controlled synthetic tasks are used to validate this account. A data deviation kernel estimates errors and predicts changes in quantity mass for real diffusion sequence models. The paper compares dataset and interface interventions and reports that transforming the generator’s coordinate system effectively reduces quantity drift.

sections.text:
Egocentric human video offers a scalable source of manipulation priors for robot learning, yet translating raw data scale into generalizable robot policies demands rigorous data curation and training recipes.

We introduce Open-HumanWAM, the first fully open recipe for scaling egocentric pretraining to 50,000 hours, anchored by Open-HumanWAM-50K---a curated egocentric video corpus densely annotated with hand motion and natural language.

Leveraging this corpus, we systematically investigate pure human pretraining via closed-loop simulation evaluations and uncover an empirical log-linear scaling law linking pretraining data hours to downstream robot success rates.

Grounded in these findings, we develop HumanWAM-Vanilla, a world--action model pretrained exclusively on 50k hours of egocentric human video. Upon robot post-training, HumanWAM-Vanilla reaches 92.08% success on RoboTwin 2.0 Clean2Clean and 68.88% on Clean2Random, alongside a 14.17% mean success rate and a 19.00 mean progress score on RoboDojo.

To push the capability frontier further, we explore joint human--robot pretraining with HumanWAM-Goal, a visual-goal-conditioned world--action model.

Hybrid data scaling unlocks broad zero-shot generalization across both simulation and physical benchmarks, propelling post-trained RoboTwin 2.0 performance to new state-of-the-art levels: 92.70% on Clean2Clean and a substantial leap to 84.60% on Clean2Random.

On physical robots, HumanWAM-Goal further exhibits emergent embodied in-context learning, dynamically adapting its manipulation behavior to unseen visual goals without parameter updates.

To support reproducible scaling research in embodied AI, we open-source the Open-HumanWAM-50K corpus, data curation and pretraining pipelines, alongside the pretrained and post-trained HumanWAM checkpoints, inference code, and simulation evaluation suites.

summary.en: The paper presents Open-HumanWAM, a recipe for pretraining embodied models on annotated egocentric human video. Closed-loop simulation evaluations show an empirical log-linear relationship between pretraining hours and robot success. After robot post-training, HumanWAM-Vanilla reports results on RoboTwin 2.0 and RoboDojo. HumanWAM-Goal uses joint human-robot pretraining and is reported to generalize zero-shot across simulation and physical benchmarks; on physical robots, it adapts to unseen visual goals without parameter updates. The authors say they open-source the corpus, pipelines, checkpoints, inference code, and evaluation suites.

sections.text:
Humanoid robots are expected to take over strenuous material handling in manufacturing, logistics, and healthcare, where operating existing wheeled carts would let them move heavy loads without modifying the workplace.

However, humanoid cart pushing remains challenging because the bimanual grasp closes a force-coupled loop in which the contact wrenches that drive the cart also disturb the robot's balance, and payload changes alter the coupled dynamics.

We propose ForPC, a force-aware whole-body control framework that regulates cart velocity through two-stage reinforcement learning. A locomotion prior is first trained under varied hand loads and upper-body postures to provide balance support.

A force latent and a state latent are then inferred from onboard observations, without external force sensors, and fed to a residual policy that coordinates bounded arm, waist, and leg adjustments with base-velocity commands.

Multi-objective rewards penalize bimanual internal opposition, grasp slip, and actuator saturation, encouraging the policy to apply contact force on demand without human demonstrations.

Sim-to-sim experiments show that ForPC reduces cart-velocity RMSE by up to 68.2% relative to a locomotion-only baseline (Loco-only) and cross-track RMSE by up to 74.2% on the multi-bend route.

Trained solely in simulation, the policy also transfers to a physical Unitree G1 without real-world training or fine-tuning and, with no payload-specific adjustment, pushes a cart carrying up to 30 kg at 0.5 m/s. These results suggest that humanoid robots could eventually replace humans for efficient material handling in daily life.

summary.en: The paper presents ForPC, a force-aware whole-body control framework for humanoid cart pushing. It first trains a locomotion prior under varied hand loads and postures, then infers force and state latents from onboard observations to guide a residual policy coordinating limb adjustments and base velocity, without external force sensors or human demonstrations. Sim-to-sim experiments report lower cart-velocity and cross-track errors than a locomotion-only baseline. The authors also report that a simulation-trained policy transfers to a physical Unitree G1 and pushes a loaded cart without real-world training or fine-tuning.
summary.zh: 论文提出 ForPC，一种用于人形机器人推车的力感知全身控制框架。该方法先在不同手部负载和上身姿态下训练运动先验，再根据机载观测推断力和状态潜变量，以残差策略协调手臂、腰部、腿部调整及底盘速度指令，且不使用外部力传感器或人类示范。仿真对比显示其降低推车速度和横向跟踪误差。作者还报告，仅用仿真训练的策略迁移至实体 Unitree G1，无需真实训练或微调，可推动载重推车。

items.title: ForPC: Force-Aware Whole-Body Control for Precise Humanoid Cart Pushing

sections.text:
Applying an imitation learning policy to a new manipulation task usually requires collecting new demonstrations and retraining the model, which makes sample efficiency a practical concern.

Pretraining on large-scale robot datasets is effective in this respect, but such datasets are costly to collect and train on, while data augmentation techniques typically require a new round of data generation and retraining for each task.

A complementary question is what useful prior can be provided to a policy at negligible cost before any task-specific data are collected. In this study, we construct a geometric visual pretraining dataset in which each scene contains only a plane, an object, and a hand, and trajectories are generated automatically.

The scenes contain neither textures nor backgrounds; pretraining primarily exposes the policy to the geometric relationship between the hand and the object. Furthermore, representing the hand as a cube avoids tailoring the dataset to a specific robot morphology.

We evaluate this geometric prior using ACT on three simulated robots across five manipulation tasks each, as well as on three real-world robot tasks.

Across many of these robot--task combinations, fine-tuning from the geometric prior achieves higher success rates in the early stages of training than training from scratch while using only a small number of task demonstrations.

These results suggest that even highly simplified geometric scenes can provide a useful initialization that transfers across robots and to real-world tasks when task data are limited.

summary.en: The study tests whether inexpensive geometric pretraining can help manipulation policies before task-specific demonstrations are collected. The authors automatically generate texture-free scenes containing a plane, an object, and a cube-shaped hand, then evaluate ACT on three simulated robots across five tasks each and on three real-world robot tasks. They report higher early-training success than training from scratch in many robot-task combinations when using few demonstrations. The evidence is limited to these simulations and real-world tasks.
summary.zh: 本文研究如何在收集任务示范前，为操作模仿学习提供低成本几何先验。作者自动生成仅含平面、物体和立方体手部的无纹理场景及轨迹，用其预训练策略，再以ACT在三种仿真机器人各五项任务和三项真实机器人任务上评估。作者报告，在许多机器人与任务组合中，少量任务示范下从该先验微调，训练早期成功率高于从头训练；结果提示简化几何场景可能帮助跨机器人迁移，但证据范围限于所述仿真与真实任务。
